from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 8  # sources
    J = 7  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [194, 98, 184, 120, 205, 104, 182, 167]
    demands = [36, 39, 55, 34, 59, 12, 32]
    cost_matrix = [[27.04, 6.16, 17.67, 22.42, 5.36, 23.67, 25.57], [5.68, 22.09, 15.92, 22.18, 22.52, 4.34, 28.12], [15.37, 29.02, 21.22, 3.24, 21.82, 24.66, 25.45], [19.8, 26.37, 4.28, 7.74, 16.22, 17.29, 5.98], [22.0, 18.01, 8.93, 24.09, 19.79, 13.29, 23.3], [7.47, 24.48, 27.43, 20.09, 18.74, 7.42, 5.27], [6.84, 8.41, 20.51, 21.49, 17.32, 18.18, 19.92], [18.46, 28.08, 11.67, 11.92, 4.19, 4.36, 24.79]]
    emission_matrix = [[12.16, 20.0, 18.76, 11.54, 9.72, 16.23, 13.99], [9.31, 10.5, 11.02, 14.0, 1.62, 10.08, 1.0], [11.95, 3.36, 6.07, 10.2, 4.58, 14.71, 12.66], [9.33, 6.15, 16.02, 7.36, 8.22, 14.48, 18.18], [2.96, 14.87, 11.41, 3.79, 4.49, 18.51, 17.6], [5.18, 2.14, 14.53, 13.84, 12.5, 16.93, 12.96], [7.78, 11.35, 2.44, 9.03, 7.45, 10.67, 9.34], [18.49, 13.5, 17.55, 3.51, 10.14, 14.09, 9.75]]
    fixed_costs = [[226, 285, 138, 214, 80, 271, 284], [255, 88, 159, 210, 126, 256, 58], [226, 66, 183, 66, 289, 216, 121], [129, 166, 168, 89, 241, 150, 100], [203, 94, 283, 94, 169, 246, 299], [259, 88, 293, 227, 294, 51, 230], [164, 209, 54, 211, 59, 288, 163], [119, 181, 93, 68, 277, 113, 177]]
    moq = [[10, 9, 16, 9, 16, 6, 5], [11, 19, 18, 20, 14, 12, 16], [5, 17, 5, 18, 20, 12, 11], [12, 16, 9, 7, 17, 5, 12], [8, 20, 16, 12, 9, 18, 10], [14, 5, 13, 12, 18, 9, 19], [11, 9, 10, 19, 18, 5, 20], [17, 14, 5, 13, 9, 5, 5]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Leadership Team  
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director  
Date: Current period  
Subject: Balancing shipping cost and carbon impact under operational realities

Context
Our network moves products from multiple warehouses to multiple retail locations. Each possible warehouse‑to‑store lane carries two performance signals: a monetary cost per unit and a carbon emission rate per unit. In practice, the least‑cost lanes often come with higher emissions, while cleaner options can be more expensive. We need a shipping plan that responsibly balances our financial targets with our sustainability commitments without compromising service.

Operational rules we must honor
- Route activation and setup costs: Turning on any lane requires a one‑time setup charge for contracts, paperwork, and physical readiness. A lane is either used or not used in a given plan. If used, the setup charge applies regardless of how much we ship on that lane.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: Once a lane is activated, we must ship at least a specified minimum volume to justify carrier commitments and avoid partial loads. This prevents “sampling” a lane with trivial quantities.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive deliveries from at most a set number of warehouses. This reflects receiving dock capacity, scheduling discipline, vendor management simplicity, and contractual arrangements. It ensures predictable inbound flow and reduces operational complexity at the stores.

Supply and demand guardrails
- Warehouses have finite available inventory. Outbound shipments from any warehouse cannot exceed what is available there.
- Stores have minimum demand that must be met within the planning horizon. All stores must be covered, and no store should fall short of its requirement.

Management priority
Leadership has set the relative importance of cost versus emissions for this plan. Variable shipping dollars and total emissions will be combined using these weights to reflect our balanced priorities. Importantly, the one‑time setup charges for any lane we activate will be added in full and are not scaled by these weights. This approach makes the trade‑offs transparent while keeping fixed onboarding decisions visible in the total.

Planning goal
We will identify which lanes to activate and how much to ship on each active lane so that:
- No warehouse ships more than its available inventory.
- Every store’s minimum demand is met.
- Any activated lane carries at least its required minimum order.
- Each store draws from no more than the allowed number of supplying warehouses.
- The blended total is as low as possible, where the blended total equals:
  • Weighted variable shipping cost across all flows, plus  
  • Weighted total emissions across all flows, plus  
  • The full setup cost for each activated lane.
This plan will be presented with clear trade‑offs, including expected spend, expected emissions, the set of active lanes, and volumes by lane. We will also test scenario sensitivity to the management weights and the supplier limit to understand how the plan shifts as priorities evolve.

Next steps
- Confirm data for warehouse supplies, store demands, lane‑level variable costs, lane‑level emission rates, lane setup costs, minimum order quantities, and the maximum number of supplying warehouses per store.
- Build candidate plans that respect the operational rules and compare them on the blended total and service robustness.
- Review with leadership to validate the preferred balance of cost and emissions for the current period and lock the route activations.
